parameters.excerpt: The current standard only supports PMLEN=XLEN-48 (i.e., PMLEN=16 in RV64) and PMLEN=XLEN-57 (i.e., PMLEN=7 in RV64). A setting has been reserved to potentially support other values of PMLEN in future standards.
parameters.reasoning: PMLEN is a direct implementation parameter that determines how many upper bits are masked. The spec defines only two legal values (16 and 7 for RV64), making this an enumerated choice.

parameters.excerpt: Pointer masking only applies to RV64. In RV32, trying to enable pointer masking will result in an illegal WARL write and not update the pointer masking configuration bits
parameters.reasoning: The implementation chooses whether to support pointer masking on RV32. The spec says it 'only applies to RV64' but this is a design choice - implementations could theoretically support it on RV32.

parameters.excerpt: Profiles and implementations may choose to support an arbitrary subset of these extensions and must define valid ranges for their corresponding values of PMLEN.
parameters.reasoning: Implementations choose which pointer masking extensions (Ssnpm, Smnpm, Smmpm, Sspm, Supm) to support. This is a subset selection from the defined set of extensions.

parameters.excerpt: Trying to enable pointer masking in an unsupported scenario represents an illegal write to the corresponding pointer masking enable bit and follows WARL semantics.
parameters.reasoning: The pointer masking enable bits are WARL fields where implementations define which combinations of privilege modes and PMLEN values are legal. Unsupported combinations result in the write being ignored.
